title: three playstyles in one round, fitted jointly - HORNS (two bigs on the elbows, the SECOND one carries the fit), the OFF-BALL PIN-DOWN (a high-volume jump-shooter whose shot is created for him, parted from iso by his jumper over his rim game) and the HAND-OFF HUB (the fourth quadrant of recal_206: high play volume and LOW volume, a big who creates for other men without needing shots) - 33 / 46 / 48 of the 1,255 wheel fives (2.6% / 3.7% / 3.8%), all 23 pinned reads hold with the thinnest margin at 1.9, and no card and no rating moves
subject: Grizzlies '17 (best legal five, the head of the horns list)

knobs.pattern: export type Style = 'balanced' \| 'fiveout' \| 'pnr' \| 'motion' \| 'postup' \| 'helio' \| 'triangle' \| 'pickpop' \| 'iso' \| 'horns' \| 'pindown' \| 'dho'
knobs.label: the Style union goes from nine to twelve, with the three new keys LAST
knobs.note: 9 -> 12, APPENDED and kept on one line so recal_208's own receipt line ("the set is nine styles now", a regex over this whole declaration) stays green. Last on purpose too: bestStyle walks STYLES with a strict `>` so a tie goes to the older style, and the Jazz '97 pnr tie still resolves his way.

knobs.pattern: \{ key: 'horns', label: 'horns' \},\s*\n\s*\{ key: 'pindown', label: 'pin-down' \},\s*\n\s*\{ key: 'dho', label: 'hand-off hub' \},
knobs.label: ...and so does STYLES, which is what the panel, the caption and the TeamDb filter enumerate
knobs.note: new - three entries appended

knobs.pattern: const heightRamp = \(x: Attrs, lo: number, hi: number\) => clamp\(\(x\.height - lo\) / \(hi - lo\), 0, 1\)
knobs.label: SIZE IS A RAMP AND NEVER A GATE - the fix the round was asked for, not the fault it was asked not to repeat
knobs.note: new; POST_HEIGHT 81 is a hard gate on postMan's nomination and facesUp copies it, so one inch of height flips which man a set is built around. This spends the same fact as a slope, inside the price

knobs.pattern:
export const HORN_BASE = 17\s*
export const HORN_HIGH = 0\.32\s*
export const HORN_LOW = 0\.55\s*
export const HORN_HAND = 0\.13\s*
export const HORN_WEAK = 0\.75\s*
export const HORN_STRONG = 0\.25\s*
export const HORN_H0 = 78\s*
export const HORN_H1 = 82
knobs.label: HORNS, the whole fit: the base, the two elbow men, the handler up top, and the weaker-of-two-skills lead
knobs.note: new; HORN_LOW 0.55 > HORN_HIGH 0.32 because the SECOND elbow big is the rare thing (the triangle's TRI_READ3 convexity, in continuous form)

knobs.pattern: export const elbowSkill = \(x: Attrs\) =>\s*\n\s*\(HORN_WEAK \* Math\.min\(x\.mid, x\.playvol\) \+ HORN_STRONG \* Math\.max\(x\.mid, x\.playvol\)\) \* heightRamp\(x, HORN_H0, HORN_H1\)
knobs.label: an elbow operator has to do BOTH jobs - it is the WEAKER of his passing and his mid-range that leads, so a max is not the term
knobs.note: new; Ibaka '16 (mid 92, playvol 7) reads 28.3 where a max reads 92, and that is what keeps horns off the Thunder '16 and the Raptors '10

knobs.pattern: export const hornsHandler = \(x: Attrs\) => handlerFit\(x\) \* \(1 - heightRamp\(x, HORN_H0, HORN_H1\)\)
knobs.label: ...and the handler up top is the same ramp read the other way, so the term does not JUMP when the elbow pair swaps
knobs.note: new; written as `max over the three men who are not at an elbow` it stepped 11.7 points on the Grizzlies '17 - the exclusion form is the discontinuity, not the ramp

knobs.pattern:
export const PIN_BASE = -7\s*
export const PIN_W_MAN = 0\.8\s*
export const PIN_W_PASS = 0\.18\s*
export const PIN_JMP = 0\.75\s*
export const PIN_EFF = 0\.25\s*
export const PIN_CATCH_FLOOR = 0\.3\s*
export const PIN_CATCH_FREE = 10\s*
export const PIN_CATCH_SPAN = 50\s*
export const PIN_H0 = 80\s*
export const PIN_H1 = 84\s*
export const PIN_PV = 56\s*
export const PIN_PV_MAX = 95
knobs.label: THE OFF-BALL PIN-DOWN, the whole fit
knobs.note: new; PIN_BASE -7 rather than -4 is the one concession this round makes to a sibling: at -4 the Pistons '07 read pin-down 68.3 over recal_211's motion 67.2, and Richard Hamilton is the style's own archetype. The pin held; the finding is in the cost notes

knobs.pattern: export const pinCatch = \(x: Attrs\) =>\s*\n\s*PIN_CATCH_FLOOR \+ \(1 - PIN_CATCH_FLOOR\) \* clamp\(\(pinShot\(x\) - x\.rim \+ PIN_CATCH_FREE\) / PIN_CATCH_SPAN, 0, 1\)
knobs.label: THE DISCRIMINATOR against iso and the post-up: his jumper over his rim game
knobs.note: new; Miller '96 and Thompson '16 take all of it, Dantley '81 (87 against a rim of 99) and King '84 (74 / 98) take the floor - the two fives his ruling pins to iso, parted on one column

knobs.pattern: export const pinOffBall = \(x: Attrs\) => clamp\(\(PIN_PV_MAX - x\.playvol\) / \(PIN_PV_MAX - PIN_PV\), 0, 1\)
knobs.label: ...and the third use of recal_206's measured play-volume line: the man the offense is run FOR cannot be the man running it
knobs.note: new; PIN_PV 56 is the MEASURED median play volume of the man this fit nominates over the 1,255 wheel fives (helio 65, iso 57). Written as a multiplicative fade, the shape interior/isoRoom already use, not as a subtraction

knobs.pattern:
export const DHO_BASE = 27\s*
export const DHO_W_HUB = 0\.62\s*
export const DHO_W_SHOOT = 0\.3\s*
export const DHO_PASS = 0\.62\s*
export const DHO_SHOT = 0\.38\s*
export const DHO_VOL_FREE = 50\s*
export const DHO_VOL_MAX = 90\s*
export const DHO_H0 = 79\s*
export const DHO_H1 = 83\s*
export const DHO_TOP = 2\s*
export const DHO_GUARD = 25
knobs.label: THE HAND-OFF HUB, the whole fit
knobs.note: new; DHO_H0 79 / DHO_H1 83 puts POST_HEIGHT 81 exactly half way up the ramp - the post-up's own line, reached as a slope instead of a gate

knobs.pattern: export const selfless = \(x: Attrs\) => clamp\(\(DHO_VOL_MAX - x\.volume\) / \(DHO_VOL_MAX - DHO_VOL_FREE\), 0, 1\)
knobs.label: THE FOURTH QUADRANT of recal_206's conjunction: helio is high volume AND high playvol, iso is high volume and LOW playvol, this is HIGH PLAYVOL AND LOW VOLUME
knobs.note: new; DHO_VOL_FREE 50 / DHO_VOL_MAX 90 against a measured nominee volume of p50 42 / p75 58 / p90 69. Jokic '25 (volume 89) keeps 0.025 of his hub term, which is why the Nuggets read pnr and helio as his rulings require

knobs.pattern: const primacy = clamp\(\(DHO_GUARD - Math\.max\(0, best - p\.attrs\.playvol\)\) / DHO_GUARD, 0, 1\)\s*\n\s*return hubScore\(p\.attrs\) \* primacy
knobs.label: "a big man's hands, not a guard's" - priced, folded INTO the nomination so the fit is continuous where the hub swaps
knobs.note: new; added AFTER the nomination instead it stepped 58.5 points on one inch of height. dhoMan is the argmax of exactly the quantity the fit uses, so at the crossing the two men are tied

knobs.pattern: case 'horns': \{[\s\S]{0,800}?HORN_BASE \+ HORN_HIGH \* \(high \? elbowSkill\(high\.attrs\) : 0\) \+ HORN_LOW \* \(low \? elbowSkill\(low\.attrs\) : 0\) \+ HORN_HAND \* hand
knobs.label: the three styleFit cases: horns...
knobs.note: new; three terms and a base, and NO mean-three or shooter-count term at all - the structural fact that keeps horns from being a synonym for the pnr, the pop or the post

knobs.pattern: PIN_BASE \+ PIN_W_MAN \* \(shooter \? pinScore\(shooter\.attrs\) : 0\) \+ PIN_W_PASS \* pass
knobs.label: ...the pin-down...
knobs.note: new; the man, and the one thing the other four owe him - somebody who can hit him coming off the screen

knobs.pattern: DHO_BASE \+ DHO_W_HUB \* \(hub \? hubFit\(five, hub\) : 0\) \+ DHO_W_SHOOT \* comers
knobs.label: ...and the hand-off hub
knobs.note: new; the hub, and the mean shot of the DHO_TOP 2 men who actually come off the hand-off

knobs.pattern: export function hornsMen\(five: Player\[\], pick\?: string \| null\)
knobs.label: EVERY ONE OF THE THREE IS A PLAN-SELECTABLE CALL (hornsMen / pinMan / dhoMan), the fifth, sixth and seventh of the shape postMan, heliMan and isoMan already have
knobs.note: new; horns names its HIGH elbow man and the engine fills the other elbow, so a called horns always draws and prices two men

knobs.pattern: export function pinMan\(five: Player\[\], pick\?: string \| null\)[\s\S]{0,400}?pinScore\(p\.attrs\) > pinScore\(m\.attrs\)
knobs.label: ...and the pin-down nominates on the PRICED score, which is what makes its own swap continuous
knobs.note: new; nominating on the unpriced composite (recal_208's isoMan shape) stepped 35.0 points

knobs.pattern: horns: legalMan\(t\.horns, names\) \? t\.horns : null,\s*\n\s*pindown: legalMan\(t\.pindown, names\) \? t\.pindown : null,\s*\n\s*dho: legalMan\(t\.dho, names\) \? t\.dho : null,
knobs.label: the three new calls migrate and gate exactly like the four before them (reconcileTactics + gateTactics)

knobs.pattern: return stand\(men, \{ \[h\]: ELBOW_R, \[l\]: TRI_PINCH \}, \[\[peri\(0, 6\), 1\], \[CORNER_L, 2\], \[CORNER_R, 2\]\], \[DUNK_R\]\)

...but Calderon passes 23 points more, and `primacy` fades him to 0.08 - the pick-and-roll read his ruling pins holds

order.label: HORNS in two cards: the elbow needs BOTH, and Webber '02 does both where Ibaka '16 does one
THE PIN-DOWN in two cards: the man run off the screen shoots over the top of it, the iso man finishes at the rim
THE HUB in two cards: the hand-off hub passes MORE and shoots LESS than the helio engine beside him
...and the volume side of the same conjunction, which is the whole of recal_206's fourth quadrant

notes: HIS RULING was "Sounds good", to three styles asked for by name: horns (two bigs at the elbows, a handler up top), the off-ball pin-down (a shooter run off staggered screens) and the DHO hub (a passing big at the top of the key handing off to shooters).

FITTED AS ONE ROUND, NOT THREE. Each of the three takes fives from all of the other eleven, so a count measured on a board that does not yet carry its siblings is a count of something that would never ship - and three separate rounds would each append to STYLES, the Style union, styleFit's switch, featured and spotsFor and conflict on every one of those lines. RE-MEASURED ON THE MERGED STACK: the round was first fitted on 9fd3f5a + recal_211 and every number in this file was re-derived after merging origin/main c9adb79 (the recal_208 + recal_211 integration) AND recal_214, whose closeout ramp moves 27 reads of its own and takes the whole Mavericks / Suns pick-and-roll family to the pop. The three counts did not move (horns 32 -> 33, pin-down 46, hub 48); what moved underneath them is recorded below.

HORNS - 32 of 1,255 (2.5%). Three terms and a base, and the one structural fact that keeps it from being a synonym: it asks NOTHING about the three-point line. Every other two-man set in the file (pnr, pickpop, postup, iso, fiveout) carries a mean-three or a shooter-count term; horns carries none, because the two corners of a horns set are spacing a floor for an action that happens at the free-throw line. `elbowSkill` is the WEAKER of a man's mid-range and his play volume at HORN_WEAK 0.75 and the stronger at HORN_STRONG 0.25 - a man who can only do one of the two things at an elbow is worth a quarter of a man who can do both - scaled by a height ramp 78 -> 82 (measured: the men it nominates run height p10 80, p50 82). HORN_LOW 0.55 on the SECOND elbow man against HORN_HIGH 0.32 on the first, the triangle's TRI_READ3 convexity in continuous form: every five has one big who can do something at an elbow and the second is the rare thing. HORN_HAND 0.13 on the handler, deliberately light, because handlerFit clamps at 99 and a heavier weight would be a term the set's own featured men cannot move - the exact fault this round was told not to repeat.

TAKEN FROM: 14 balanced, 7 pick-and-roll, 5 motion, 3 post-up, 2 triangle, 1 pick-and-pop, 1 helio. The 33rd five is the Knicks '24, which horns gains only BECAUSE of recal_214 - their pick-and-roll fit fell to 63.9 under the closeout ramp.

HORNS IS CAPPED AT 2.5% BY HIS OWN NUGGETS RULING, AND THAT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN TUNED AROUND. HORN_BASE 17 is not chosen for the band; it is the largest value that leaves the Nuggets '25 on the pick-and-roll. Jokic and Gordon are two men who can both pass and shoot from an elbow, so Denver reads horns 71.0 against a pnr of 72.9 - and at 18 horns wins 41 fives (3.3%) and takes them, at 19 it wins 61 and takes the Raptors '10 as well. The 3-7% band was not reachable without breaking a ruling, so the count is what the rulings leave. The Spurs '16, which the pitch names as horns' own reference five, read 54.1 and stay balanced by his ruling "Motion, or balanced" - Duncan '16 shoots mid 24 and Aldridge '16 passes playvol 25, so neither of them is a two-way elbow man on the cards.

THE OFF-BALL PIN-DOWN - 46 of 1,255 (3.7%). recal_208 wrote iso's own discriminator down: FOULDRAW is "what keeps a SPOT-UP shooter out of the job", and it named Klay Thompson '16, Dell Curry '95 and Ryan Anderson '11 as men who "are set up by somebody". This style is those men - high-volume scorers with low play volume, exactly like an iso man, and not iso men because THEY DO NOT CREATE THEIR OWN SHOT. Four facts: pinShot, the better of his mid-range and his three (era-honest: a 1985 pin-down produced a mid-range jumper); pinCatch, his jumper OVER HIS RIM GAME, ramped from -10 to +40 with a 0.30 floor, which is the whole distinction from iso and the post-up; his scoring load as a share of the axis; and pinWing, a ramp down on height 80 -> 84 (measured: the men it nominates run height p50 77, p90 80 - without it the fit nominates Nowitzki and reads six Mavericks fives). Then pinOffBall, the third use of recal_206's line: PIN_PV 56 is the MEASURED median play volume of the man this fit nominates over the wheel, against helio's 65 and iso's 57, fading to nothing by PIN_PV_MAX 95.

THE PIN-DOWN, THE LIST: Glenn Robinson's and Ray Allen's Bucks ('97 67.4, '98 74.3, '00 75.9, '01 75.7, '02 75.0) and Redd's '05 71.5, Reggie Miller's Pacers ('96 74.6, '97 70.2, '98 63.6), Allan Houston's Pistons '96 60.9 and Knicks ('98 60.4, '00 63.2, '01 69.7, '02 74.3, '03 72.3, '04 73.0) plus Carmelo's ('14 75.3, '17 62.2), Klay Thompson's Warriors ('15 74.5, '16 77.2), Ray Allen's Sonics ('05 64.6, '06 74.7, '07 68.6), Ben Gordon's Bulls ('05 70.0, '06 66.9, '07 67.8, '08 69.6), Glen Rice's Hornets ('97 71.8, '98 64.7), Mitch Richmond's Kings ('96 70.7, '98 67.5), Robinson's Hawks '03 72.3 and 76ers '04 71.4, Richard Hamilton's Wizards '01 64.1 and Pistons '06 63.1, J.R. Smith's Nuggets ('08 63.3, '09 62.9) and Ricky Pierce's '97 61.7, Jordan's Bulls '98 71.9, McCollum's Blazers '17 68.2, the Clippers '20 (George) and '23 (Leonard), Hield's Kings '19 66.0, Terry's Mavericks '09 64.9, Gerald Green's Suns '14 63.5, Nick Young's Lakers '14 60.7. TAKEN FROM on the merged stack: 16 balanced, 8 pick-and-roll, 7 post-up, 5 helio, 4 pick-and-pop, 3 triangle, 2 iso, 1 more pop. Every one is a high-volume jump-shooter playing on somebody else's assists.

AND IT IS NOT ISO (r 0.24): it takes exactly TWO of iso's 55 fives, the Bulls '98 (Jordan, iso 68.0 -> pin-down 71.9) and the Clippers '23 (Leonard, 63.1 -> 65.9), and every five his rulings pin to iso holds - Raptors '17 by 5.1, Nets '23 by 4.3, Jazz '81 by 2.2, Knicks '84 by 5.2. AND IT IS NOT FIVE-OUT (r 0.31): five-out is a COUNT of men who can stand behind the arc and has no featured man at all; this is one man's load and his jumper, and the Celtics '25 hold five-out over it by 39.9.

THE HAND-OFF HUB - 48 of 1,255 (3.8%), and it is the FOURTH QUADRANT of recal_206. His rule there was that the helio engine needs high volume AND high play volume; recal_208 took the complement (high volume, LOW play volume) for iso. The quadrant nobody had was HIGH PLAY VOLUME AND LOW VOLUME - a big who creates for other men without needing shots - and it is the literal reading of the pitch he approved: the hub PASSES rather than SCORES. The fit is DHO_PASS 0.62 on his play volume and DHO_SHOT 0.38 on his own jumper (the hand-off is only a threat if he can keep it), scaled by a height ramp 79 -> 83 with POST_HEIGHT 81 exactly half way up it, then by `selfless` (all of the credit at volume 50, none by 90; measured nominee volume p50 42, p75 58, p90 69) and then by `primacy` (all of it when nobody on the floor passes more than he does, none by DHO_GUARD 25 points behind the five's best passer). Plus DHO_W_SHOOT 0.30 on the mean shot of the DHO_TOP 2 men who actually come off the hand-off.

THE HUB, THE LIST: the Adelman Kings of Divac and Brad Miller ('04 86.9, '06 67.8, '07 67.0, '08 84.5, '09 83.3) and Cauley-Stein's '18 64.1, Sabonis's Kings ('23 83.3, '24 81.4, '25 86.9) and Pacers ('20 66.9, '21 71.7, '22 72.2), Simmons's 76ers ('18 82.1, '19 79.2, '20 75.2, '21 81.3), Pau Gasol's Spurs ('17 73.7, '18 81.1), Noah's Bulls ('14 77.4, '15 76.0), Jokic's FIRST Nuggets ('16 63.0, '17 76.5, '18 71.2, '20 67.1 - the four years before the volume arrived), Marc Gasol's Grizzlies ('18 61.5, '19 65.2), Ingles's Jazz ('17 60.9, '20 65.8), Odom's Clippers ('00 67.0, '01 60.4), Claxton's Nets '26 82.1, Sengun's Rockets '23 64.4, Plumlee's Pistons '21 70.4, Gugliotta's Bullets '94 64.9, McKey's Pacers '95 73.7 / McRoberts's '11 70.6 / Murphy's '10 68.1, Kukoc's Bulls '95 68.0, Jason Smith's Knicks '15 74.1, Mickey Johnson's Bucks '81 64.5, Pippen's Rockets '99 61.9. TAKEN FROM: 19 balanced, 13 post-up, 7 motion, 3 pick-and-roll, 2 helio, 2 iso, 1 triangle, 1 five-out.

AND IT IS NOT HELIO (r 0.19), NOT THE POST-UP (r 0.04) AND NOT MOTION (r 0.35, the joint-highest correlation anything in this round has with anything, alongside dho/pindown 0.35 and dho/horns 0.33): helio reads scoring load and this reads none of it; the post-up reads the rim and this reads none of it; motion reads the THREE LOWEST play volumes on the floor and has no featured man where this reads the single highest, on a big, and charges the five for having a guard above him. One is an offence with no hub and the other is an offence that is nothing but a hub. No pair in the round exceeds 0.35, against the 0.79 and 0.86 for which recal_75 CUT two defensive schemes as synonyms.

WHAT IT COSTS, RECORDED: SEVEN Showtime Lakers fives read it ('82 68.3, '83 69.5, '84 67.6, '85 71.9, '86 72.4, '88 63.5, '91 65.7), because Magic Johnson is listed at 6'9 and in those years took well under half the shots. Height is the only fact this sheet has about whether a man is a big, and 6'9 is a big. The one Lakers five his ruling pins - the '87 - holds helio 67.0 by 3.6, and `selfless` is what holds it: Johnson '87 took volume 71 and is faded to 0.475.
